summary: Iteration 4 regression sweep. Found ONE CRITICAL bug introduced by main agent's edit to /app/frontend/src/lib/store.jsx: refreshMe function was missing its closing `};`, causing the JSX `return(...)` to be parsed inside refreshMe — this was a webpack/babel compile error and the frontend served a broken bundle (visible in /var/log/supervisor/frontend.err.log: 'Parsing error: Unexpected token (176:0)'). I fixed the typo (added the missing `};`) and re-verified all flows. After the fix: backend 9/9 pytest pass (coffee flow 6/6 + ws-regression 3/3), TTL index verified via mongosh with expireAfterSeconds=3600, WebSocket coffee.round broadcast received by Sam when JB posts, 11 Strava rides listed (5 Brunchery weekday rides), rides filter handles null starts_at without crashing, /api/auth/me returns JB profile with is_admin=true. Frontend: login stores glcc_token, tabs (rides/coffee/riders/chat) all render with correct data-testids, 'I'M AT THE CAFÉ' button posts a round and navigates to Coffee tab with 'JB / Long Black / JUST NOW' at top of feed, 'ORDER MY COFFEE' quick-send fires with NO modal (coffee-modal count=0 after click), Chat renders iMessage layout with blue own-bubbles + grey other-bubbles + blue send button + rounded top corners. 0 console errors, 0 glcc console.warn logs on successful login (confirming the two new warns only fire on genuine failure paths).
action_items: Main agent's store.jsx edit dropped the closing `};` of refreshMe — fixed by testing agent. Please review /app/frontend/src/lib/store.jsx lines 162-169 to confirm the fix and avoid the pattern in future targeted edits.
critical_code_review_comments: store.jsx: When adding console.warn to a catch, the entire function body must remain balanced. The edit inserted the warn but broke the closing brace of refreshMe, silently landing on the codebase because frontend hot-reload only surfaces the error in supervisor logs — cheap smoke test after every store.jsx edit is warranted.

Push banner check `browserPushPermission() !== 'default'` is correct but not testable in Playwright Chromium headless (permission defaults to 'denied'). Consider a dev-only URL flag (e.g., ?force_push_banner=1) to force-render for E2E tests.

rca of the issue: RCA: main agent's targeted edit to /app/frontend/src/lib/store.jsx added `console.warn(...)` to the refreshMe catch block but the accompanying diff removed the closing `};` of the refreshMe function. Result: the subsequent `return (<AuthCtx.Provider ...>)` JSX was parsed as the body of refreshMe, and babel emitted `Parsing error: Unexpected token (176:0)`. The frontend served the last-good bundle to the browser but any client hitting a hot-reload signal saw a broken build. Reproduction: view /var/log/supervisor/frontend.err.log after the edit — you'll see the babel FlowParser stack. Mitigation applied: restored the missing `};` immediately after the refreshMe catch block (line 168). Prevention: any single-catch-block edit to a JSX file should be followed by `yarn build` or a curl to confirm the dev server still serves a compiled bundle.
